import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 4

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture4

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 4](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

If `G` is a connected graph then the maximum number of leaves over all spanning
trees satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ NG(G) - 1` where `NG(G)` is the minimal neighbourhood
size of a non-edge of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture4 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    NG G - 1 ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture4

reformulations.difference: The maximum-leaf quantity is implemented as a real supremum over spanning subgraphs, rather than by explicitly selecting a maximizing spanning tree.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite connected graph, the set of spanning trees is nonempty and finite. The leaf counts are ordinary finite cardinalities, so their real supremum is attained. Consequently, for every real b, b ≤ Ls G is equivalent to the existence of a spanning tree with at least b leaves. This verifies the maximum-leaf encoding; it does not establish the attribution of the entire inequality to WOWII Conjecture 4.

could_not_verify: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture4.conjecture4: could not independently verify the exact WOWII Conjecture 4 statement, its NG conventions, or its current recorded status. The cited http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/ redirects to an HTTPS endpoint that times out; alternate-host and archival attempts did not yield the entry. The accessible DeLaViña–Waller paper confirms the maximum-leaf terminology and finite simple connected graph setting, but does not restate this particular conjecture.
review.notes: No mathematical defect was established, but the source comparison remains incomplete. Lean checks in /workspace/review/invariants.lean and computation.lean compile successfully. They verify supremum attainment, the harmlessness of the Nontrivial restriction, Ls(K₂) = 2, and the complete-graph case despite NG's default value |V|. Computations also checked NG on complete graphs, edgeless graphs, paths, and cycles through order 7. The equivalence and boundary proofs do not depend on sorryAx. No repository files were edited.
